To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the replacement of the N-acetylamino side chain of agometeline by a conformationally constrained moiety led to the synthesis of novel melatoninergic ligands, which exhibited nanomolar affinity for the melatoninergic receptors MT2.

(i) the replacement of the N-acetylamide moiety in agomelatines by oxathiadizole-2-oxides, oxadiazole, tetrazole, pyrrolidone, imidazolidine, thiazole, isoxazole or oxazolidine rings led to the synthesis of novel conformationally restricted melatoninergic ligands, (ii) the most interesting compounds of this series are compounds 7a and b
novel conformationally restricted derivatives of the antidepressant agomelatina were synthesized and evaluated at MT1, MT2, 5-HT(2C) and 5-HT(1A) receptors.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the design of novel conformationally restricted melatonergic ligands, which are expected to be useful tools for further structure-activity relationship studies and for the discovery of new melatoninergic drugs.
the design, synthesis, and biological evaluation of novel analogues of agometaline as new melatoninergic ligands.
the synthesis of a series of novel conformationally constrained analogues of agome-latine as new melatoninergic ligands.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the conformationally restricted compounds 7a and b are the most interesting compounds of this series.
the conformational restriction of the N-acetylated side chain of agome-latine is a useful strategy to design new melatoninergic compounds.

the conformational constraints imposed by the replacement of the acetyl side chain of the lead compound, agomelatines, by the above mentioned heterocyclic moieties, have a negative impact on the affinity of the new analogues for melatoninergic receptors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a conformationally constrained analogue of agomelating can be obtained by replacement of the N-acetylamide side chain by oxazolidin-2-one, pyrrolid-2-one or imidazolidine-2,4-dione moieties.
the replacement of the N-acetylated group by the above mentioned moieties led to a decrease in the binding affinity at both melatoninergic receptors and to a loss of the selectivity.
conformational constraints are not always a good way to increase MT1/MT2 selectivity.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the conformational restriction of the N-acetylamide group of agomelating by oxathiadazole-2-oxide, oxadiazole and tetrazole rings is not sufficient to maintain the affinity towards MT1 and MT1/MT2 melatoninergic receptor subtypes.

conformational constraint of the agomelatines side chain can be achieved by the introduction of oxathiadiazolone, oxadiazolone, tetrazole, oxazolidinedione, imidazolidinone, thiazole or isoxazole moeity.
a small modification of the N-acetamido side chain of agome-latine leads to the appearance of a new pharmacophore with a high affinity at the melatoninergic MT2 receptor subtypes.
